lesson.menu_desc: Narrating a Formula 1 race + present continuous vs present simple -- 27 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 9 -- Race Weekend
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Thiago Negrães | Lesson 9 -- Race Weekend

items.situation: A car pulls out and passes another one in front of you, on television, right now.
tips: Right now means the verb takes -ing.
There is one verb for passing another car.

items.situation: A friend who knows nothing about the sport asks how the starting order is decided.
tips: This is a general fact, so the present simple.
Two words name the session, one names the first place.

items.situation: The leader goes into the pits while the second car stays out.
tips: Two actions happening at this moment.

items.situation: Somebody asks how long a tyre change usually takes.
tips: Usually is the clue: present simple.

items.situation: A car stops on the grass with smoke coming out of it, five laps from the end.
tips: There is one verb for leaving the race before the end.
Say what is happening, then what it means for the result.

listenings.text: And we are on lap forty-one of fifty-eight. The leader is coming into the pits right now, which means the second car takes the lead for the first time today. Remember, a pit stop normally takes about two and a half seconds, so he is not losing much. Behind them, the fight for the podium is getting serious: the car in fourth place is overtaking on the outside, into turn one, and that is a brave move. One driver has already retired this afternoon with an engine problem.

Good afternoon and welcome to our preview of Sunday. Qualifying finished an hour ago and the grid is now set. The driver on pole position starts from the clean side of the track, which usually matters more here than anywhere else. The teams are checking the weather every ten minutes, because rain is arriving from the west. Most of them are planning one stop, but if it rains they change everything. We are back at one o'clock with the build-up to the race.

extra_audio.text: First, qualifying on Saturday decides the grid for Sunday. Then the driver on pole position leads the field into the first corner. After that, the cars come into the pits and the teams change the tyres. Next, one car overtakes on the outside and takes second place. Finally, one driver retires with an engine problem and the top three go to the podium.
